notes.title: 😺What's Noodling - Cloudheim Dev Blog #6🍝
notes.content:
[p]Hello, Runari![/p][p][/p][p][b]Here's the big news first: Cloudheim will have a demo during [url="https://store.steampowered.com/sale/nextfest"]Steam Next Fest[/url] this October![/b] That means you’ll be able to jump (back) in and play the game real soon.[/p][p][/p][p]In the meantime, the team at Noodle Cat has been hard at work diving into Open Beta feedback and making lots of improvements as we prepare for launch. This blog is all about sharing what’s new since then, so let’s get into it![/p][p][/p][h1]Open Beta Learnings[/h1][p]During the open beta, we had over [u]19,000[/u] playtesters checking out Cloudheim that weekend, sharing lots of incredible reactions, feedback, and bug reports.[/p][p][/p][p]While it was quick for our environment artists to patch up the various holes in the maps that were reported, some other feedback required a more careful approach in how we could address them. The areas we tackled the most can be put into three buckets: [b]Context[/b], [b]Comba[/b]t, and [b]Crafting[/b].[/p][p][/p][h2]Context[/h2][p]While combat will always be the highlight feature of Cloudheim, we heard from many players who loved the world so much they wanted more: more context, more story, and more details about everything.[/p][p][/p][p][i]Who are you? What is this place? What are you doing in the game, and why are you here?[/i][/p][p][/p][p]We saw that as a good sign: people are really loving the world and are hungry for more! To answer those questions, we dedicated more time to weaving in narrative elements and tying quests together in a way that better reveals the big picture.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/cc72ebf21e8a39733585d76f9eb136d45dd42536.png"][/img][/p][p]You are one of the chosen Runari, renowned figures of past legend whose powers are drawn from ancient gods that once freely roamed the lands. After Ragnarok, dark forces spread across the world, and you have been called once more to help restore balance. Using the Bifrost, you’ll descend into each area to drive out corruption, reawaken slumbering deities, and gather an eclectic cast of allies along the way. [/p][p]In addition to more narrative context, we’ve also been chipping away at better game cues and various interfaces to help players navigate the world and what’s happening at any given moment. This includes more interaction prompts and an improved quest log.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/c470fe223b9fed031f82048ac54a647826cd8710.gif"][/img][/p][p][i]An indicator will appear to tell you when you’re close enough to use a lasso point.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Overall, the work in this area should make it easier to understand your goals, follow the flow of quests, and stay grounded in what’s happening around you.[/p][p][/p][h2]Combat[/h2][p]Of course, we still made updates to combat, since it is the main draw of Cloudheim. Changes include tweaks to how damage works for a more satisfying experience overall; new animations, visuals, and sound effects for various weapon combos and skills; and a revamped armor system for enemies.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/647a4b986679ee765723ff96786ac88d8db9bf67.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]In trying to make enemies more distinct, we’ve also given some of them new movesets and abilities. For example, not only do grobb healers restore their allies…they can even resurrect fallen ones!
[/p][p]Finally, we’ve been doing some cool work with dungeons and adding in interesting puzzles and new areas for you to discover while out on your adventures.[/p][p][/p][h2]Crafting[/h2][p]We’ve saved the biggest section for last, as crafting is where a lot of significant changes happened![/p][p][/p][p]In all the playtests we’ve had, survey results showed that your base on Odin Shell needed some love. While it was easy to grasp the combat and exploration side of the game, we noticed a drop-off in interest when it came to the crafting and shop side.[/p][p][/p][p]Here are some of the notable ones:[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Weaponcrafting results are more predictable now.[/b][/h3][p]A frequent area we saw raised by beta playtesters was how weaponcrafting was handled in the game. Players found it too random and wanted more control over their outputs, so we went and expanded it out a bit more. [/p][p]The forge will have four sections, corresponding to each playable class, so you’ll be able to choose what set of weapons you craft based on where the materials are added.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Your base is now even more customizable.[/b][/h3][p]We’ve made some drastic changes to how you build out your home in the skies. Initially, the base was designed to be fairly linear. Your base upgrades resulted in a fixed building with all the related stations and decor appearing in predetermined slots, save for a handful of movable items like sales tables.[/p][p][/p][p]We decided to do away with this system and allow for more freeform placement. Rather than being stuck with only one of each station and in fixed locations, you can now purchase multiple and place them more freely.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/2d7da81d5d11b8c5e90c493293e1941535fc9233.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Of course, for those who are invested in how your base looks, you’ll still have plenty of options to decorate, with even more items and new layouts available in this system.[/p][p][/p][p]Basically, we’ve split out the features to be less intertwined, allowing you more options when it comes to optimizing your crafting without feeling constrained, or vice-versa — being able to decorate and show off your cool collections without being limited by various crafting arrangements.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]The loot box is now your central storage for items.[/b][/h3][p]Previously, you only had one option when interacting with the box: to have it spit out all your items in a flashy explosion, but then you were left with piles of items on the floor. For many testers, this felt a little too messy and overwhelming.[/p][p][/p][p]Now, interacting with the box also offers a proper menu where you can view all of the items you’ve acquired out in the world, all in one location.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/ea1824007bb608e413afd1600a06a63dae3c690b.png"][/img]As a bonus, we even added a feature where you can locate any placed item on your base — a request we saw during beta testing. [strike]Now you can find that one cheese wheel that somehow went missing.[/strike][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Blins are even more important.[/b][/h3][p]As you progress in your adventures, you’ll be able to recruit Blins and bring them to your base. They’re going to need housing, of course, but as a show of appreciation, they’ll be available to help around in various ways.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/a64aecc219fc16c2c6f7f72919d00ba8fce2d2b0.png"][/img][i]Meet Berg, one of the many blins you’ll be able to recruit. (Yes, they all have names!)[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Assign Blins to your stations to help boost production speeds, or build out specialized guild hubs to activate unique perks. For example, assigning Blins to the fishing guild can increase yields and the appearance of rarer fish at the pond in your base.[/p][p][/p][h1]What’s Next…[/h1][p]With Next Fest on the horizon, we’re excited to have players joining the skies of Cloudheim once more. Get ready for plenty of action-packed combat and exploration, building out your base on Odin Shell, and, of course, kicking greebles off cliffs. We can’t wait to see what kind of adventures you’ll create. [/p][p]See you then![/p][p] [/p]
[url=https://discord.gg/8YjPU7RUhU][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/6fdbbee50fc6632c75a7e29c911be2b0a3eabf25.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: 💫 Playtest Complete — Tell Us What You Think!
notes.content:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/b2a44c4663f4b2987b7b4b21e71f5a48f134148f.png"][/img][/p][p]Our latest playtest has officially come to a close! Thank you so much to everyone who joined and answered the call to knock down those pesky grobbs. 🥊[/p][p][/p][p]It’s been amazing seeing the feedback, bug reports, and chaos you all brought to Cloudheim, and we’re incredibly grateful for your time and support.[/p][p][/p][h2]📝 Got a minute? We'd love your feedback![/h2][p]We’ve put together a survey to help us understand what worked, what didn’t, and what you’d like to see more of. The survey will stay open until[b] July 24th at 3:00 PM ET.[/b][/p][p]
[url="https://forms.gle/yhThCnqjFhuUS5ec7" style="button"]👉 Take the Survey Here[/url][/p][p][/p][p]This is just one step in the journey — and thanks to your help, the next one will be even better.[/p][p]Until next time!🌼
[/p][p]— Noodle Cat Games[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/6fdbbee50fc6632c75a7e29c911be2b0a3eabf25.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Open Beta Starts Now!
notes.content: [p]Hello, brave Runari![/p][p]It’s time — our Open Beta weekend playtest has started![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/7df761cbb9edbb22e26dbc82de39e32075adebb5.gif"][/img][/p][p]You can jump in [b]right now[/b] and start exploring islands, tackling dungeons, crafting in your base, and bonking Grobbs to your heart’s content.[/p][p][/p][h1]✨How to Participate[/h1][p]1. Navigate to the Cloudheim Store Page:[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2070270/Cloudheim/"][/dynamiclink]2. Click on "Request Access" in the Join the Cloudheim Playtest section on the page.[/p][p]3. You should be automatically granted access![/p][p][/p][h1]📌Things to Know for Open Beta[/h1][p]Here are some important things to know as Open Beta is just around the corner! [/p][p][/p][h2]💎Game State[/h2][list][*][p]The Open Beta version of the game will have limited content up to a certain point - you'll be done once you've unlocked and explored [spoiler]all of Arcadia.[/spoiler][/p][/*][*][p]As the game is still actively being developed, please anticipate bugs, incomplete content, placeholder assets, and other unintended wonkiness (a bonus with our physics combat :P)[/p][/*][*][p]We've also added a new game mode (with two versions) that even closed beta testers haven't seen![/p][list][*][p]You can access the Combat Bowl/Chaos Bowl via the Demos tab at the start of the game, or through a portal when you unlock your base on Odin Shell.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Localization is currently not in the game, but will be added in the future. (The settings menu might have partial translation, but it's not comprehensive for the whole game.)[/p][/*][*][p]The game is not optimized for Steam Deck and is not officially supported at the moment (you might experience crashing)[/p][/*][*][p]There is controller support, keyboard rebinding, and co-op cross-platform support between Steam and Epic Games.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h2]🪄What’s Available[/h2][h3]Exploration[/h3][list][*][p]Beginning Tutorial Experience[/p][/*][*][p]Odin Shell - Your home in the skies.[/p][/*][*][p]Arcadia Outlands - A streamlined area.[/p][/*][*][p]Arcadia (Mainland) - The first major island available.[/p][/*][*][p]5+ discoverable dungeons (some with multiple layouts!)[/p][/*][*][p]A new game mode: The Combat Bowl, and its more difficult variant, the Chaos Bowl[/p][/*][/list][h3]Combat[/h3][list][*][p]8 appearance options: Astrid, Jaxel, Joree, Kai, Maeve, Mana, Revna, and Rurik[/p][/*][*][p]4 class options: Runeblade, Breaker, Sentinel, Ranger[/p][/*][*][p]Over 40 unlockable weapons, skills, lasso types, and kick options to equip[/p][/*][*][p]10+ different enemy types and their variants, from pesky Greebles to the hulking Troggs[/p][/*][/list][h3]Base[/h3][list][*][p]3 phases of available Shop upgrades[/p][/*][*][p]Freeform placement for crafting stations and decor[/p][/*][*][p]Weapon Crafting, Fishing, and Shopkeeping[/p][/*][/list][h2]🔮What's Planned (in the Future)[/h2][list][*][p]More combat improvements[/p][/*][*][p]More shop content[/p][/*][*][p]More appearance options[/p][/*][*][p]New islands[/p][/*][*][p]Localization support[/p][/*][*][p]More performance optimizations[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h2]🪲 Notable Known Issues[/h2][p][i]Note: This is not an extensive list.[/i][/p][list][*][p]Some crafters may only be placed by the host in a multiplayer game; this is not intended and a bug relating to quest requirements[/p][/*][*][p] ⚠️ [b]Items placed on shelves or tables will not update or move when you upgrade your base.[/b][/p][list][*][p]It’s [i]highly[/i] recommended to clear out items away from the main shop area to avoid losing access to these items.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Items placed on storage shelves or sales tables may not behave properly after leaving and coming back to the base[/p][/*][*][p]Enemy names or sometimes levels may display incorrect information[/p][/*][*][p]It’s possible to lose your equipped loadout when respawning or traveling to new maps, which should be resolved by equipping it again[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h2]🐞 Bug Reports[/h2][p]We have an in-game bug-reporting feature! This is the✨ [b][i][u]preferred method[/u][/i][/b] ✨ to report bugs as it will automatically send tons of useful info to us. It can be accessed via the menu or by using the shortcut F8 on the keyboard.[/p][p][/p][h2]💌Feedback[/h2][p]An optional survey will be shared after the playtest ends. We've also set up some Discord channels for open beta.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/f7407d18efbd7f08a350b1780e3fe2614642bc30.png"][/img][/p][p]Whether you’re here to test the systems, dive into combat, or just see what Cloudheim’s all about, thank you for being part of the journey! We can’t wait to hear your thoughts about the game.[/p][p]See you on Odin Shell!🪽[/p][p]— Noodle Cat Games[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/6fdbbee50fc6632c75a7e29c911be2b0a3eabf25.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: 😺What's Noodling - Cloudheim Dev Blog #5🍝
notes.content:
[p]What’s up, everyone![/p][p][/p][p]For this blog, we’re putting the spotlight on the characters and creatures that bring the world of Cloudheim to life. Some you’ll be able to play as right away, some you’ll be able to recruit in your journey, and some, well, are creatures looking to stir trouble.[/p][p][/p][p]Oh, and if you haven't already, make sure to check out our latest trailer here:[/p][previewyoutube="6zpbPzsDYVc;full"][/previewyoutube][h1]💫Bridge New Worlds as the Runari[/h1][p]You play as a Runari: powerful beings with a connection to the Gods in the world before Ragnarok. They were gifted with the ability to channel mystical powers, thus shaping the course of history. But when the Gods disappeared, so too did the Runari… until now. What does it mean for them to return?[/p][p][/p][p]At the start of your journey, you’ll choose from a handful of playable Runari: Meet Maeve, Jaxel, Rurik, and Mana — with a couple more characters you’ll see if you play Open Beta this weekend![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/e443cdf638a30bcb116cb8b299c35b7690839f09.png"][/img][/p][p]Note: Characters in Cloudheim are cosmetic. You’ll be able to choose whoever you want to play as, while the skills you bring to the table are fully customizable during gameplay.[/p][p][/p][p]As you travel across the islands and brave the dungeons, you’ll also meet and unlock new characters. Meet Tilda, the Blacksmith; Brooks, the (Accidental) Chef; and Grove, the Gardener.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/fc8aae10adb0fbbfe5d2009e51b37fdf9f444f53.gif"][/img][/p][p] With each shop upgrade and area expanded in your base, you’ll bring on more allies ready to help you with your journey.[/p][p][/p][h1]🐑Discover Friends and Foes[/h1][p]It’s not just people populating the world of Cloudheim — you’ll be running into all kinds of whimsical creatures. Some are helpful, while others are... a little more chompy.[/p][p][/p][p]Around your base, you’ll see Gnasher, a resource-hungry [i]something[/i], who’ll happily take your unwanted items in exchange for rewards. You'll also be able to recruit Blins, tiny helpers for your store that can help boost productivity.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/35ee62df812554fd6691db1300f359941e872d13.gif"][/img][/p][p]On the enemy side, you’ll run into a wide assortment of colorful and threatening foes. For example: Grobbs, who are mischief incarnate. These invaders might look harmless, but their goal is total conquest, and they leave plenty of corruption in their wake. Make sure to wipe out grobb forts and encampments before they grow too powerful![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/d18d441b3012bddf271522bd116f7da115e9deb5.png"][/img][/p][p]You’ll also find Corvin: cloaked spellcasters tied to ancient dark magic, and their rituals threaten to awaken something far worse. As they’re flying creatures, you’ll have to change up your strategy. Shoot out a ranged projectile or lasso them down to earth to deal even more damage![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/97c0da0303bf1c4f6b94eba085e5eb994dabc6ab.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Watch out if you run into a Trogg  — these hulking, one-eyed creatures love to stomp around with some flashy attacks, and have a penchant for showmanship. You might even see them toss a nearby ally as a ranged attack![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/6c79a596c825771d51d60609df84dcc57839d4f9.gif"][/img][/p][p]Look forward to these enemies and more as you venture forth and restore the world! 🗺️[/p][p][/p][h1]📣Community Corner[/h1][p]During our closed beta playtests, some testers uncovered silly bugs that were just too fun not to share! Here’s a video with a round-up of our favs:[/p][previewyoutube="5-hk_6Reacg;full"][/previewyoutube][p]1. [b]A New Perspective[/b] - When doing a downward kick in a certain way, your character might end up seeing things from a new angle. [/p][p]2. [b]Shelf Rider[/b] - Who knew freeform decorating also meant an alternative way to travel around?[/p][p]3. [b]Backup Blins[/b] - Yes, we have emotes in the game. Turns out the Blins didn’t want to be left out, either.
[/p][p]Thanks to the playtesters who discovered and shared them with us! 😀[/p][p][/p][h1]🏃Up Next…[/h1][p]What’s next is actually the Open Beta playtest! This will be your chance to jump into Cloudheim and experience the world firsthand, and we'll be sharing more details as we get closer to the weekend. See you soon! ♥️[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/6fdbbee50fc6632c75a7e29c911be2b0a3eabf25.png"][/img][/p]

[b]Playtest period:[/b] [b]Friday, July 18th[/b] 12pm ET - [b]Monday, July 21st[/b] 12pm ET 

Oh, and check out this trailer we made 👀
[/p][previewyoutube="6zpbPzsDYVc;full"][/previewyoutube][p]We will share more details on how to join the playtest on Steam soon! To stay up to date with the latest playtest details, join the community on the [url="https://discord.gg/cloudheim"]official Discord server.[/url]

notes.title: 😺What's Noodling - Cloudheim Dev Blog #4🍝
notes.content:
[p]Hey there, fine felines![/p][p][/p][p]Our newest trailer premiered at IGN Live recently, but in case you didn’t see it, take a look here:[/p][previewyoutube="FLDoTVlV7Yk;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]This blog is all about the vibrant world of Cloudheim! Discover new lands as you and your friends explore the islands and delve into monster-filled dungeons. Let’s get into it![/p][p][/p][h1]❤️It Starts (and Ends) at Home[/h1][p]At the heart of every adventure lies your base. Perched atop Odin Shell, it’s where you’ll gear up, make plans, and set off through the mysterious Bifrost gate to explore the islands below.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/573e6b5a0d86e7704b9fe86faae86e207a4523ff.png"][/img][/p][p]When your journey ends, it’s time to bring it all back — and it's a good thing loot is automatically collected, isn’t it? Once you’re home, you can refine materials, craft new weapons, and stock your shop with goods to sell. This is where your progress takes shape and where the next journey begins.[/p][p][/p][h1]🗺️Explore a Fractured World[/h1][p]Cloudheim takes place in a world broken apart by the events of Ragnarök. As such, the overworld maps in the game are separated as islands, which you travel through thanks to the powerful magic of the Bifrost Waygate.[/p][p][/p][p]You’ll explore grasslands overtaken by grobb tribes and their wooden encampments…[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/7948b2955b288a70dfc781a59010baccb3171986.png"][/img][/p][p]…a desert where an ancient god slumbers…[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/b19344ca2f8fd31726ac11cf741fd439429a1a3b.png"][/img][/p][p]…and a winter domain full of abandoned mines and castle ruins.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/82b7654b98125d16dfac8039ad21036fd6cb4092.png"][/img][/p][h1]💎Dangerous Dungeons & Rewarding Ruins[/h1][p]As you explore the islands, you’ll discover entrances to dungeons brimming with both enemies and treasure alike.
[/p][p]Encounters are often layered with puzzles, environmental hazards, and locked areas that call for clever use of your tools and skills.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/50569da5e259460e06ebb15aa15f0b609b29847c.png"][/img][/p][p]Treasure chests packed with valuable loot are scattered throughout, rewarding curious explorers who stray from the beaten path. In Cloudheim, it’s not just about reaching the end; it’s about everything you uncover along the way.[/p][p][/p][h1]🪩Q&A Time![/h1][p]We brought in some folks from the team to chat about level design and world-building.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/03ba3a21886e24651c99bc557268684783b56a5d.png"][/img][/p][p][b]When it comes to world-building, what does “show, don’t tell” mean to you?[/b][/p][p][/p][p][b]Ian:[/b] It means treating the player intelligently. I'm always considering how to balance the guidance the player needs for their goals against the least amount of guidance needed to make things feel vast and immersive. Exploration is my favorite aspect in games, so I know how good it feels to slowly piece together an understanding of an area and the lore surrounding it. It's like a giant puzzle![/p][p][/p][p][b]John:[/b] To me, “show, don’t tell” is about making the world feel lived-in through its design, not its dialogue. A ruined bridge can suggest a fallen kingdom. A sun-drenched clearing after a claustrophobic cave can imply safety or relief. Good world-building invites the player to observe, speculate, and feel—not just listen. When done right, even the quietest corner tells a story that feels personal, because the player discovered it rather than being told about it.
[/p][p][b]Wojtek: [/b]It's the best method of storytelling, whether you're a writer, a filmmaker, or a game designer. It's also the most expensive, as it requires scripting sequences, animating objects, adding visual and audio effects, and other similar tasks.[/p][p]To get a little technical, in Cloudheim, we designers have a fantastic tool at our disposal—the signal system. This in-house technology allows us to script a sequence of events quickly, visualize all the connections, and debug them efficiently. The system lets us create building blocks and reuse them.[/p][p]We've developed modules that detect player presence, track where the player is looking, switch effects on and off, change materials on objects, and more.[/p][p][/p][p][b]How do you account for different player behaviors, like those who like to rush through versus the ones searching every corner?[/b][/p][p][/p][p][b]Ian:[/b] I do my best to make areas multifaceted but still cohesive. Giving a clear goal, adding a puzzle, unique combat encounters, and a ton of little secrets ensures that everyone has something to do, but they can still run straight to the end of an area if that's their playstyle.
[/p][p][b]John:[/b] It’s a question of rhythm and affordance. Some players want to express mastery through speed. Others want to express it through thoroughness. As designers, our job is to ensure both feel seen. That can be through visual signposting, branching flows, or soft pacing shifts—moments where the game invites a deeper look without demanding it. Ultimately, it’s about respecting player agency while still guiding the experience.
[/p][p][b]Wojtek:[/b] Always need to ensure we have things for both player types - ideally a golden path that is easy to find and follow for people who want to rush through, and many cool things and secrets to discover for people who enjoy exploring.
[/p][p][b]What are some things to consider when designing a dungeon, especially for a co-op game?[/b]
[/p][p][b]Ian:[/b] I want dungeons to hold value for players because they feel like truly different experiences, so it's important to me that dungeons have a unique theme for their gameplay, story, and art. Everything from the enemies that spawn to the foliage on the walls should make a space feel unique and satisfying to explore. My hope is that the variety is something players will notice and appreciate as a team.
[/p][p][b]John:[/b] A couple things come to mind, but perhaps most importantly, you want moments that test the group as a group. Not every challenge needs to be hard individually, and some of the most rewarding moments come from timing, coordination, and shared tension. A great co-op dungeon lets players feel like they pulled something off together.
[b] [/b][/p][p][b]If you had to pick just one favorite area (without too many spoilers!), what would it be?[/b]
[/p][p][b]Ian:[/b] There is a particularly bouncy corner in our desert with a lot of destruction and a unique puzzle. I love that place![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/0b75236198351d94b9f5a62bbd68a4d6fee775ce.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Wojtek:[/b] [i](Had the same answer as Ian.)[/i] It is a perfect mix of an interesting space with a lot of movement options, dynamic combat, impressive visuals and challenging puzzles.[/p][p][/p][p][b]John:[/b] Without spoiling too much? It’s an area where the environment shifts in a way that changes how players move through it. That’s where the magic is.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/f7407d18efbd7f08a350b1780e3fe2614642bc30.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]This is just a glimpse of what goes into creating a world like Cloudheim’s, and we can’t wait for players to begin their adventures and discover what’s in store![/p][p][/p][h1]📣Community Corner[/h1][p]Did you know we’ve been running some playtests? notes.title: 😺What's Noodling - Cloudheim Dev Blog #3🍝
notes.content:
Hey everyone! 

We just shared our latest trailer, showing the heart of your base: the crafting and shop system that takes place on Odin Shell.

In case you missed it:

[previewyoutube=tPTp3O404hA;full][/previewyoutube]
[h1]⚙️Hands-On Crafting[/h1]

What’s unique about the crafting in Cloudheim is that there are no menus! All the loot you’ve collected while out on your adventures is stored in a magical chest. From there, you interact directly with stations: toss ores into the forge, drop meat on the grill, or line your shelves with finished goods to sell. All of this happens in-world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/95011d25d70d16285485d690701295e6c637671b.gif[/img]

Loot is shared party-wide, and this applies to anything you craft as well. Newly forged weapons are unlocked for everyone, so no need to worry about fighting over that rare dagger or crafting it three times over. As you discover more items, you’ll get stronger, learn new skills, and improve your combat capabilities — just in time for your next expedition!

[h1]🧺Your Shop in the Skies[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/54d94d311a13951e71da4fdea348c5a35e7ebbbc.png[/img]
Crafting isn’t just for equipment: you’re also running a store and meeting the needs of visitors from distant lands. Customers will come and go with various requests, and fulfilling them earns you more gold and reputation.

Expand out your base with new areas such as the garden, which can grow herbs, and then use those plants in the alchemy nook to craft potions to sell. Or maybe build out the kitchen, cooking up tasty dishes like tomato soup and grilled skewers to serve to your hungry patrons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/c8f98d0b703e2cc09f435804e766a205aca94241.png[/img]
Keep your store well-stocked and word will spread. Soon enough, you’ll have a bustling little corner of the sky to call your own.

[h1]🪩Q&A Time![/h1]

For this Q&A, here are the folks whose work helped shape this portion of the game:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/49cb43876643881cce9677b3079d7a9ede793cf2.png[/img]
[h3]It’s interesting that this game has a shopkeeping component. Was this always the vision?[/h3]

[b]David:[/b] We always knew we wanted to make a game that had both combat and shopkeeping, but it wasn’t clear how much of a mix it would be.

[b]Kim:[/b] As a design goal, we wanted to focus on content that was fun to play with a group of friends. As we continued developing the game, the shopkeeping aspect evolved to complement and enable more fun combat.

[h3]How does the crafting portion of the game fit with the action and exploration side?[/h3]

[b]Kim:[/b] Exploring and defeating enemies is the “gathering” phase of the game, while crafting is the “production” side that allows for personal and team-wide improvements, both materially in the items you can equip, but also passively via stat increases from certain upgrades and expansions. So, crafting improves your future expeditions by making you more efficient at defeating enemies and faster at exploring.

Crafting also supports player agency in our game. As you craft and unlock more gear, you can choose to bring exactly what you want into battle and explore different playstyles and loadouts. You can also choose to be an efficient shopkeeper with a system in place, [i]oooor[/i] you can just throw things on shelves and call it a day!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/9d6cc596a7c36bade950d392491b81709308f92f.png[/img]
[h3]How do you approach designing a crafting system with no menus?[/h3]

[b]Kim:[/b] It can be a challenge for sure! As designers, we’re constantly thinking about things like, “Does this match with what players expect with the systems of this world?”, “Are the crafting stations intuitive enough to use without too much instruction?”, and “Are players able to get what they need in a balanced way?”

[b]David:[/b] Sometimes you’ll come up with something that seems fun on paper, but ends up being more of a chore when implemented.

[b]Kim:[/b] When done successfully, it’s great to see players enjoy something when “It Just Works(™).” No need to look up a guide or wiki. The way our crafting works matches our combat — both are very hands-on and keep you involved with the game world.

[h3]How do these features add to the cooperative feel of the game?[/h3]

[b]David:[/b] So, we didn’t intentionally go about making a no-menu crafting system. It came out of trying to figure out a way to allow friends to craft together. Menus tend to conflict with that.

[b]Kim:[/b] There’s an old story called “Stone Soup” where everyone is throwing together ingredients. Our crafting system is like that, where a group of people can work together to make cool stuff. With multiple crafters, you can coordinate who takes on what, and make lots of different items as a result.

Also, your store isn’t the only thing on Odin Shell. I encourage exploring every nook and cranny in our game! As a designer, I love being able to hide little treasures, puzzles, and other activities throughout the map. I want to give players the ability to play together and have fun in interesting ways.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/9abcd33ec477d668fe3043323bc1eaa844ec2806.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/f7407d18efbd7f08a350b1780e3fe2614642bc30.png[/img]
Whether you're out adventuring or crafting back at your base, Cloudheim is what you make of it, especially together with friends!

[h1]📢A Quick PSA[/h1]

It’s not too late to sign up for our Closed Beta Playtests! The first wave of invites will be going out SOON™…

[url=https://cloudheim.firstlook.gg/?utm_source=steam&utm_campaign=cb_announce&utm_content=blog]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/b4a4cac6f71c92e3896e4883af1b5fe03c281b18.png[/img][/url]

[h1]🗺️Up Next: Islands & Dungeons[/h1]

With our next blog, we'll be covering the vast biomes and maps that you can explore in Cloudheim. From frosty castles to sandswept tombs, we can't wait to show more of this world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/5386faae058d0245d56332741098d8fb2cfa4831.png[/img]
See you then!

[url=https://discord.gg/8YjPU7RUhU][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/6fdbbee50fc6632c75a7e29c911be2b0a3eabf25.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: ⛅Closed Beta Signups Are Live!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/0943a93ad4de5b3a8b1738850232c4e4a3ef8041.jpg[/img]
Hi everyone!

The team has been hard at work on the game, and we’re now officially taking signups for Cloudheim’s Closed Beta period.

Cloudheim is a co-op game set in a colorful fantasy world, combining physics-based combat with crafting and base management. If you're looking for some fast-paced action with a dash of downtime, this is your chance to be a tester and have your feedback shape the game!

We’d love to get more eyes on Cloudheim and hear your thoughts. Sign up now to be a part of our upcoming playtests!

[h1]🖊️How to Sign Up[/h1]

[url=https://cloudheim.firstlook.gg/?utm_source=steam&utm_campaign=cb_announce&utm_content=blog]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/b4a4cac6f71c92e3896e4883af1b5fe03c281b18.png[/img][/url]

[list]
[*]Signing up will add you to the waitlist until we start rolling out invites.
[*]Details will vary depending on tests, and more specific information will be sent to invited testers.
[*]Make sure to check your inbox, including Spam/Promotion folders!
[/list]
[h1]❓FAQ[/h1]

[b]Why am I being required to sign into Discord?[/b]
A lot of playtest communications will be happening in our server, so we've made it an initial requirement to participate.

[b]Do I have to connect my Steam and/or Epic Games account?[/b]
We're running different playtests on different platforms, so if you want to increase your chances of being invited, we recommend both.

[b]When are the playtests happening?[/b]
Details will vary depending on the test. Invited playtesters will receive confirmation emails with more info.

[b]What happens if I don't get in? Do I need to sign up for each playtest multiple times?[/b]
Some of our tests will be looking for only a small pool of players, and the requirements will be different with each one. If you don't get into one, that's okay! [u]You only need to sign up once to stay in the pool for future invites.[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/f7407d18efbd7f08a350b1780e3fe2614642bc30.png[/img]

We can’t wait to share the game and hear your thoughts. For the latest playtest news, such as dates and invite waves, make sure to join our Discord server. 👇

notes.title: 😺What's Noodling - Cloudheim Dev Blog #2🍝
notes.content:
Hellooo cool cats,

Welcome to the next edition of [i]What’s Noodling[/i], our dev blog for Cloudheim! In case you missed it, we recently premiered our new combat trailer at the Future Games Show Spring Showcase. You can check out the video here:

[previewyoutube=WYf070uR9UI;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]🍀Squad Up with 4 Playable Classes[/h1]
Cloudheim offers four playable classes, each bringing unique strengths to the battlefield.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/a43519f2bfcb1ffd024662e747404fc095cc03dc.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] The [b]Spellblade[/b] weaves physical attacks together with magical abilities. Cast down a crash of lightning or lay down a healing aura to turn the tide of battle!
[*] The [b]Outlander[/b] favors big, heavy-hitting attacks, striking down foes to expose their weaknesses and wearing down enemy armor.
[*] The [b]Treasure Hunter[/b] jumps in and out of battle with their swift movements, always on the lookout for vulnerabilities to maximize their next attack.
[*] The [b]Sentinel[/b] brings both defense and utility to the field, with skills that can summon tools, buff allies, and knock around enemies to change up the playing field.
[/list]
All four classes in Cloudheim allow you to experience the robust combat system in different ways. We wanted to hit a wide spread of interests and playstyles, resulting in the classes you see here.

Of course, you’re not locked into any one choice  — any unlocked weapon and skill is yours to freely equip and mix around. Try switching things up: how about launching a grobb with your hammer and then blasting them with a beam?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/3d0651a4639745eded781c89849c4a7d1f117476.gif[/img]

[h1]🪩Q&A Time![/h1]
We managed to wrangle some of our team's game designers and gained some insight into what goes into designing an action game like Cloudheim. Take a look!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/ec05557d5ce6c438043fc562f7c3a97477b6ebf5.png[/img]

[h3]Why an action game?[/h3]

[b]David:[/b] I love survival-craft games and play all of them. But, most of them are set in dark worlds with a slower, more strategic approach to combat. This felt like a great opportunity to make a game in a genre I love while doing something different, and really focus on the moment-to-moment experience and how it feels to use skills in combat.

[b]Kevin:[/b] Something we wanted to avoid was “window overload” where more of your time is spent in UI menus than really experiencing the world and its gameplay. It’s like having you and your friends show up to a party but everyone whips out their phones. The hope with Cloudheim is that we can capture the fun of exploring, looting, and crafting in a more immersive way.

[h3]What would you say makes Cloudheim’s combat unique?[/h3]

[b]Kevin:[/b] One thing we agreed very early on was to make combat the differentiating factor compared to other games in this space. With our team, we really wanted to bring more elements that are usually seen in fighting games into the project. For example, the sense of timing and flow you get from a combo in real-time — and being able to remix it as you go depending on the flow of battle. Or how addicting it is to try juggling an enemy in air as long as possible. We've spent a lot of time trying to give the player a strong sense of control over combat, and aimed to make it easy for anyone to go cook up a combo. We want each new fight to feel like you're about to create another chaotic masterpiece.

[b]Ivan:[/b] With Cloudheim, the chaotic and physical nature of each engagement means you’re always adjusting your moves on the fly. Even if you come in with an idea of what combo you want to execute, odds are you’ll be changing it up depending on how the battle goes. Blink, and you might miss a good opportunity to juggle an airborne Grobb.

[b]David:[/b] There’s a system in the game called Mana Burn, where you can keep casting skills even on cooldown, but at a cost. Do it too often, and you enter a state that has your movement greatly reduced, and any next attack can K.O. you. Stronger spells naturally fill up the bar faster, so there’s an added layer of decision-making that comes with this kind of risk-and-reward mechanic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/97ea9f7370756e05ada15ef2f71ecde000c7c23a.gif[/img]

[h3]Are there any challenges in making this kind of game that people might not realize?[/h3]

[b]David:[/b] Starting out, we weren’t even sure if it was possible to make this game. Having fluid, combo-driven combat in a peer-to-peer multiplayer environment was certainly a big undertaking.

[b]Ivan:[/b] The playable characters in this game are very powerful. Monsters can easily be tossed and juggled around. When trying to design enemies that can still feel threatening despite this, some choices might be at odds with our combat values. It’s a worthwhile challenge to find that balance!

[h3]Any gameplay tips for players?[/h3]

[b]David:[/b] There’s a lot of room to leverage the animation cancelling in our game. Try mixing different attacks together, such as throwing a thunder spear in the middle of a weapon combo — if you press fast enough, you’ll still be able to complete the attack chain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/f7407d18efbd7f08a350b1780e3fe2614642bc30.png[/img]

There you have it! We hope players have as much fun with our combat system as our team has had in developing it.

[h1]🌠Community Spotlight[/h1]
Can you guess which of the four classes is the most popular so far? We polled across our communities and the winner is…

🥁Drumroll, please… 🥁

[i][b]…the Spellblade![/b][/i]

Here is a breakdown of the results:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/6aaf6ca9fbd89fb26a781638ccccab88431470f5.png[/img]
[h1]🔨Up Next: Crafting![/h1]

Running around the world and conquering dungeons is fun, but eventually you gotta bring all that loot to your base. We’ve covered the action part of our action-craft game… you already know what’s coming up!

Our next trailer will dive into the mechanics of blacksmithing, shopkeeping, alchemy, and more.

As a teaser, here’s an NPC mid-contemplation. Which potion do you think they’ll buy?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/b9b1c08d34be1f090431c9544ff01efc8cef1c4e.png[/img]
Stay tuned!

notes.title: 😺What's Noodling - Cloudheim Dev Blog #1🍝
notes.content:
Hello, everyone!

Thank you so much for all the interest and support as we announced Cloudheim for the first time. The team here at Noodle Cat is super excited for what's in store, and we are here to kick things off with our very first Dev Blog!

[img alt="A character kicking open a treasure chest with the words Dev Blog appearing inside."]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/6aab12273fc1460b355f0d2cb8d7b135deeb8b5d.gif[/img]

[h1]⁉️FAQ Round-up[/h1]
Here are some of the most common questions we’ve gotten since the game’s reveal.

[b]Q: Will there be a demo?[/b]
A: Yes! We also plan to have playtests leading up to the game's launch. Expect more news on this soon.

[b]Q: Can I play singleplayer?[/b]
A: Yes, you can play solo. Each world save will also have various settings such as experience gain and enemy difficulty that you can tune to your preferences.

[b]Q: How is multiplayer handled?[/b]
A: Multiplayer is peer-to-peer hosted. Right now, we don’t have plans for dedicated servers.

[b]Q: Is there crossplay support?[/b]
We are looking into it, but can’t guarantee crossplay support just yet.

[b]Q: Will the game release in Early Access?[/b]
At this time, we don't have plans for it to be in Early Access.

[b]Q: How much will the game cost?[/b]
We don't have a set price to share at the moment, but expect Cloudheim to be a one-time purchase — no free-to-play models or subscriptions.

[b]Q: Is it an open-world game?[/b]
Not exactly. Cloudheim has more of a hub system where you have your core base, with locations to explore and more unlocked as you progress. That said, some of the maps are pretty big!

[b]Q: Can I play as different characters?[/b]
A: Yes! While there won’t be a character creator, you’ll be able to unlock and play as different characters.

[img alt="A character looking out to a desert scene that features a colosseum atop a floating rock island held by chains."]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/ff0930c89883876c01f3a905008a5ee989ec8529.png[/img]

[h1]🌅How It All Started[/h1]
Now, let’s go back to the beginning, before there was a game or even an Unreal project set up…

From the start, we knew we wanted to make something unique. At Noodle Cat, our founding team drew inspiration from playing games across different genres over the years. “We would play survival games, fighting games, management games, and see things we could bring together to make a new kind of experience,” says David, our CEO.

That’s why it’s hard to fit Cloudheim into any one category. It’s not strictly an ARPG, nor a survival game, nor is it a base-builder. Instead, we’re calling it an “action-craft” game, where the core loop is about using fast-paced, combo-driven combat to defeat enemies and explore the world, while bringing back loot to your base to craft and unlock even more playstyles for your next adventure.

We also wanted the world setting to be something more whimsical and fun, rather than being dark or punishing.

[img alt="A magical statue with blue glowing lights set in a forest scene at night with a waterfall behind."]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/ff9d83090f4e114bd784f2b7a6de51b5318f684d.png[/img]
This playfulness is reflected not only in our art direction, but with the gameplay itself. You can kick greebles out of a cannon, feed ore into a chomping smelter, and open treasure chests with your magic lasso.

And while we do want Cloudheim to be a game that’s easy to pick up, there’s still plenty of room for those looking for a challenge as well. If all you want to do is dive into a mob of monsters and swing around a hammer — go for it! If you’d prefer tactfully chain together combos or time the perfect block with your shield, you can do that too.

[img alt="A character flourishes a sword, then performs several teleporting slashes with a purple effect at an enemy."]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/4069773f37656c1515e1f74c9c8d519cf7eaa4fe.gif[/img]

Or maybe you’re the type to take the reins back at base. If sorting inventory and managing the store is more of your jam, there’s something for you as well! We wanted to make a game where the whole family and friend group can play together.

[h1]🌠Community Spotlight[/h1]
This is the section where we usually highlight some of the really cool stuff from our community! But since things are just getting started, we’ve decided instead to share some creations from the Noodle Cat team ourselves. Enjoy. ✨

[img alt="A recreation of the fire Elmo meme using a flame grobb."]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/769deb06c2fc90f08ba350ee24be82b8198a94dd.png[/img]
[i]My computer when someone sets off 20 explosive barrels.[/i]

[img alt="A recreation of the Apu spills his tendies meme but with a little green grob."]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/b1bc5637b1c4596b2fc28aedfbd921f0db920338.png[/img]
[i]Are we the baddies?[/i]

[img alt="A character's face fades into a 'chadface' meme version."]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/e976934aae946548e28e615835ab688c4746dce4.gif[/img]
[i]“Yeah, that’s me in the trailer.”[/i]

[img alt="A simple MS Paint drawing of Odin Shell and a little hut on his shell."]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/0335a8edb4b1c406a943ccda4b26d373c649ee63.png[/img]
[i]“Hear me out… your house is ON the flying turtle.”[/i]

[img alt="A recreation of the Kung Fu Panda Tai Lung meme where a grobb is pointing up. The first panel says 'Finally! A worthy opponent!' The second panel says 'Our battle will be legendary!'"]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/95c185c444f12fdd3cce1aa4d90ea1d440417cc6.png[/img][i]That level 2 grobb when the squad shows up.[/i]

[h1]🚂Up Next: All About Combat[/h1]

Welcome aboard the hype train, because we’re just getting started! We’re excited to announce that Cloudheim will be in the [b]Future Games Show Spring Showcase[/b].

[url=https://www.futuregamesshow.com/?utm_source=steam&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=cloudheimfgs][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/19373908b0353ab2cc4e1686db42e3c18a314ae1.png[/img][/url]

Tune in [b]March 20th[/b], 1 pm PT/4 pm ET/8 pm GMT as we unveil a [i]brand new trailer[/i] covering more on the combat of Cloudheim — including classes, weapons, and enemies!💥

Here’s a quick teaser:
[img alt="A party of three characters attacking and using abilities at a giant tree enemy."]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/13d43b058b89eea300056447962edd5cd4f0924f.gif[/img]

See you then!

[url=https://discord.gg/8YjPU7RUhU][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45480286/6fdbbee50fc6632c75a7e29c911be2b0a3eabf25.png[/img][/url]

notes.content:
[previewyoutube=5ZEDgd2J3xM;full][/previewyoutube]

Coming to PC, Playstation 5, and Xbox Series X/S, you can now wishlist Cloudheim — a co-op action RPG blending crafting with chaotic physics-based combat. Gather your allies, craft your weapons, and upgrade your shop in the sky to bring harmony to a broken realm.
